name: The signed-in competitor
description: The join on live_sessions is the revocation check, and it is a join rather than a guard task so it costs no extra round trip and cannot be omitted by mistake. It yields no row for a session that has been signed out -- or for a valid token whose user has been deleted -- and `deny` refuses that case first: a condition-gated terminal task is how a workflow refuses a request while choosing its own status, and it has to be 401 because the shell maps 401 to anonymous and every other status to an error panel. (`halt_on: "failure"`, new in Orion 1.6, would stop the run but answer 400.) Postgres builds the response: the `body` column is json_build_object, and since Orion 1.6 a json column decodes as the document itself, so the respond task copies it into data.body. SOMA-GAPS 3.2: this is also where last_seen_at is kept. /v1/me is the one route the shell calls on every page, which makes it the closest thing the API has to `the session was used`, and the UPDATE is bucketed to five minutes so the ordinary request writes no row at all. It runs AFTER `deny`, so a revoked session cannot mark itself alive on the way out.

input.query: SELECT json_build_object('id', u.id, 'handle', u.handle, 'display_name', u.display_name, 'role', u.role, 'created_at', u.created_at, 'candidates', coalesce((SELECT json_agg(json_build_object('model_id', m.id, 'game', g.slug, 'version', m.version, 'phase', CASE WHEN m.status = 'testing' AND m.admit_started_at IS NULL THEN 'queued' WHEN m.status = 'testing' THEN 'verifying' ELSE 'awaiting_trial' END) ORDER BY g.slug) FROM models m JOIN games g ON g.id = m.game_id WHERE m.owner_id = u.id AND m.status IN ('testing', 'verified')), '[]'::json)) AS body FROM users u JOIN live_sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id AND s.sid = ($2)::uuid WHERE u.id = ($1)::uuid
UPDATE sessions SET last_seen_at = now() WHERE sid = ($1)::uuid AND last_seen_at < now() - interval '5 minutes'
